grade-prepare-fixture-pending.reason: Adopt for #237, part of #156 (delivery plan, slice 7, decision 6), porting grade.py prepare, preflight --offline and check_prepared to bench-tools grade prepare, preflight-inputs and check-prepared. No caller moves; grade.py stays the production command until slice 10 and is deleted in slice 11. Changes behavior on purpose, under decision grade-prepare-runner-identity-v2, which lists exactly what differs: runner_deviation, the missing validator/tools/ and the hashes that pin them. Old behavior: grade.py prepare copied grading_validation.py, claim_grading.py, pre_existing_grading.py and check_manifest.py into WORK/validator/tools/, pinned each in the key's validator beside inputs.json, and wrote runner_deviation as the version 1 object of the 23 runner-file hashes, the execution policy and the Codex catalog, which this case's baseline_defect records. New behavior: bench-tools writes validator = {"inputs.json": sha256}, creates no validator/tools/, and writes runner_deviation = {"version": 2, "files": the 23 runner-file hashes plus "rust/bench-tools": the running executable's SHA-256, "bench_tools": its rust_runtime.py pin, "execution_policy_sha256", "codex_catalog_sha256", optional "provisioning"}, which the structured identity rule labels so both implementations compare. Rationale: the Rust validator is part of the pinned executable, so copying Python validators would pin code that no longer validates. Compatibility impact: grade.py map accepts a v2 key and grade.py dispatch refuses it with the runner-changed line, since the executable is no runner file it hashes (grade-prepare-v2-key-rows); v1 keys keep Python's checks in both implementations (grade-prepare-v1-key-checks). Resolving issue: #237.

grade-prepare-unicode-16-digit-source-li.reason: Adopt for #237, part of #156 (delivery plan, slice 7, decision 6), porting grade.py prepare, preflight --offline and check_prepared to bench-tools grade prepare, preflight-inputs and check-prepared. No caller moves; grade.py stays the production command until slice 10 and is deleted in slice 11. Records an intended difference from older interpreters. bench_tools::grade::source reads \d from pytext's Unicode 16.0 decimal table, generated from Python 3.14. Old behavior: grade.py's SOURCE_PREFIX used the running interpreter's Unicode database. Under CI's Python 3.12 (Unicode 15.0), \d misses the 80 digits Unicode 16.0 added, such as U+16D70, so the first private attempt directory stays in the review and the validator inputs, which this case's baseline_defect records with Python 3.12's result; under Python 3.10 (Unicode 13.0) 110 digits are missed. Python 3.14 matches bench-tools except for the fields grade-prepare-runner-identity-v2 lists, so the differential under 3.14 reports this case as an unexplained difference. New behavior: as Python 3.14. Rationale: one table for every interpreter. Compatibility impact: attempt ids are written as att- and ASCII digits, so no saved review links such a path. Resolving issue: #237.

grade-prepare-arguments.reason: Adopt for #237, part of #156 (delivery plan, slice 7, decision 6), porting grade.py prepare, preflight --offline and check_prepared to bench-tools grade prepare, preflight-inputs and check-prepared. No caller moves; grade.py stays the production command until slice 10 and is deleted in slice 11. Changes behavior on purpose. Old behavior: argparse refused the missing option with its usage and 'the following arguments are required: --run', exit 2, which this case's baseline_defect records. New behavior: clap refuses it with its own wording and usage, exit 2. Rationale: #215's clap parsing, which every bench-tools command shares. Compatibility impact: only the usage wording changes; the exit status stays 2. The abbreviated options run the provisioner in both, which bench-tools starts as python3 where grade.py started sys.executable; the masked interpreter path is <python> in both. Python 3.12 and 3.14 agree. Resolving issue: #237.

grade-prepare-provisioner-invalid-output.reason: Adopt for #237 (acceptance criterion 5), part of #156 (delivery plan, slice 7, decision 6). Changes behavior on purpose when a --provision command fails with output that is not UTF-8. Old behavior: grade.py prepare runs the provisioner with subprocess.run(text=True, encoding="utf-8"), which raises UnicodeDecodeError before the exit status is checked, so prepare exits 1 with a traceback and leaves clone, clone-cache and clone-work in the work directory, which this case's baseline_defect records. New behavior: bench-tools grade prepare keeps the provisioner's raw output and exit status, removes all three directories and exits 2 with the command, its exit and the last 2000 characters of the output, writing each byte that is not UTF-8 as \udcXX, the surrogate escape Python's stderr writes with backslashreplace and the rendering bench-tools already uses for undecodable bytes on stderr. Rationale: criterion 5 requires a failed provisioner to leave no clone, clone-cache or clone-work and to report its exit and output tail; a decode failure defeats both and leaves a work directory the next prepare refuses. Compatibility impact: only a failing provisioner whose output is not UTF-8 changes. A provisioner that succeeds still has its output decoded strictly as UTF-8, as grade.py does, and a failure with UTF-8 output keeps grade-prepare-provisioner-fails. Python 3.12.15 and 3.14.7 show the old behavior. Resolving issue: #237.
